messages:
Maria (seceng): Heads up — analytics-sa started decrypting KMS key 'prod-events' ~12:20 UTC after today's RBAC refactor. Logs show ~1.2k Decrypt calls in the last 30m.
Dave (infra): omg, is that the key used for PII exports?
Maria (seceng): yes, it's used by the analytics pipeline for joined PII lookups. Not supposed to have Decrypt.
Chen (sre): @Irene can you check who/what principal is making the calls? need token vs service account distinction.
Irene (platsec): pulling audit logs now. Quick query I ran: `SELECT principal, action, ts, resource FROM audit.kms WHERE key = 'projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/prod/cryptoKeys/prod-events' AND action = 'Decrypt' ORDER BY ts DESC LIMIT 200` — most calls are `serviceAccount:analytics-batch@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com`.
deploy-bot: Deploy 2026-03-20T12:05Z: rbac-mapping-service @ prod-a (sha: a1b2c3) — mapping update applied.
Maria (seceng): that aligns with the deploy time. looks like the new mapping gave analytics-batch the "read-only-plus" role which mistakenly includes `kms.cryptoKeyVersions.useToDecrypt`.
Dave (infra): mitigation options: 1) revoke kms permission from read-only-plus role and roll back mapping; 2) revoke the service account binding; 3) rotate key. Which do we do first?
Chen (sre): prioritize containment: remove the permission at role level so any other principals with that role lose Decrypt immediately. After that, rebind only the intended principals.
Irene (platsec): I'm executing a targeted removal: `gcloud iam roles update read-only-plus --remove-permissions kms.cryptoKeyVersions.useToDecrypt` — doing now.
Maria (seceng): noted. also create temporary alert rule: when Decrypt on prod-events > 5/min send page.
Irene (platsec): update done — permission removed from role. Confirming metrics: Decrypt rate dropped from ~40/min to ~1/min (likely retries).
Dave (infra): good. next: revoke tokens/short-lived creds for analytics job to be safe and plan key rotation window.
Chen (sre): revoking service account keys now for analytics-batch (no long-lived keys found), forcing job restart.
Maria (seceng): can we also add an automated smoke test in the RBAC CI that runs a dry-run audit (simulate policy bindings + list of sensitive perms) to detect permission expansion?
Irene (platsec): yes — add to action items. I'll file INC-2026-128 and follow up with a timeline for key rotation and a postmortem.
deploy-bot: Incident created INC-2026-128: "Unexpected KMS decrypts by analytics after RBAC mapping change" — assigned to Irene, Dave.
Dave (infra): immediate action log: revoked permission from role, rotated analytics SA tokens, created alert. Next action: schedule key rotation for prod-events within maintenance window.
Maria (seceng): for postmortem let's include: RBAC mapping smoke tests, explicit permission allowlists per role (deny-by-default for KMS), and a pre-deploy audit diff that verifies no new principals gain KMS Decrypt.
Irene (platsec): adding remediation tasks to the security backlog and scheduling a demo of the CI check for the infra team tomorrow.
Chen (sre): all good here. marking thread resolved for now. Thanks for the quick triage. :thumbsup:
